packet.description: One TASK*.md file under /home/palantirkc/work at directory depth 1 to 3; key is the path below the work root. start_item.description: queued to in_work; repository and branch both or neither; the item must be named by its task's board.

submission_criteria.message: Choose a queued item.
Name the item in its task's order first.
Supply repository and branch both or neither; an item that held a repository takes one again.

release_item.description: in_work back to queued with a reason (a unit closed without a merge).

submission_criteria.message: Choose an in-work item.

close_item.description: in_work to done: with a repository, a closed accepting review of the task and repository that closes no other item; without, evidence.

submission_criteria.message: Choose an in-work item.
A unit closes with its accepting review; other work with evidence.
Name a review no other item names.

drop_item.description: Drop an item that is not done, with a reason.

submission_criteria.message: Choose an item that is neither done nor dropped.

set_order.description: Replace a task's order in one action; the first call creates the board (key: the task's key, by convention of the caller).

board.description: Id of type board whose native_key is the task's key.

submission_criteria.message: Choose an existing task.
Name this task's board, or a new one when the task has none.

triage_decision.description: Triage a row of the user once: item, intent, not_adopted or none.

submission_criteria.message: Choose a current row decided by the user.
A row is triaged once.
Triage item names an item of the row's task.
Triage intent names an objective of the row's task.
Triage not_adopted and none carry a reason.
Give item only with the word item and objective only with the word intent.

record_request.description: Record one message of the user that orders, decides, prefers, corrects, stops, answers or delegates, in the user's own words. It starts current and unrouted; then route it to an intent (route_request, draft_intent) or set it aside.

words.description: The user's own text in the user's language, unchanged. No action changes it: a correction is a new request (supersede_request).

words_verified.description: True when a program read the words from a session record; false when an agent wrote them otherwise. Set once: verified words replace unverified ones only through supersede_request.

truncated.description: True when the words were cut to fit 24,000 bytes; the record holds the whole message.

record.description: The session record the words were read from (a path, with a line or id), so a reader can check them.

reading.description: What the agent took the message to mean, in English: the order, decision or answer in a sentence or two.

kind.description: order, decision, preference, correction, stop, answer, or delegation: the user hands the confirmation of named intents to the Lead for a time the user does not step in.

topic.description: A short label that groups related requests (view requests_by_topic); not unique.

said_at.description: When the user said it, UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ); never later than the time of recording.

session.description: The session in which the user said it.

runtime.description: The CLI that held the session, such as claude or codex.

legacy_decision.description: Only when carrying a user's decision row of version 9: that row. Omit it for a new message.

submission_criteria.message: Give the user's words; an empty text is no message.
said_at is after now: give the UTC time the user said it. A local time written with Z can lie in the future.
legacy_decision must be a decision with decided_by user; omit it for a new message.
A request already carries this decision; find it (view requests_by_topic) instead of recording it again.

supersede_request.description: Correct a current request: it becomes superseded and a new current, unrouted request carries the corrected words. A request that confirmed an intent is corrected after amend_intent of that intent, which clears the confirmation.

words.description: The user's own text in the user's language, unchanged. No action changes it: a correction is a new request (supersede_request).

words_verified.description: True when a program read the words from a session record; false when an agent wrote them otherwise. Set once: verified words replace unverified ones only through supersede_request.

truncated.description: True when the words were cut to fit 24,000 bytes; the record holds the whole message.

record.description: The session record the words were read from (a path, with a line or id), so a reader can check them.

reading.description: What the agent took the message to mean, in English: the order, decision or answer in a sentence or two.

kind.description: order, decision, preference, correction, stop, answer, or delegation: the user hands the confirmation of named intents to the Lead for a time the user does not step in.

topic.description: A short label that groups related requests (view requests_by_topic); not unique.

said_at.description: When the user said it, UTC (YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ); never later than the time of recording.

session.description: The session in which the user said it.

runtime.description: The CLI that held the session, such as claude or codex.

submission_criteria.message: Name a current request; a superseded one was replaced: use the request that supersedes it.
Give the user's words; an empty text is no message.
said_at is after now: give the UTC time the user said it. A local time written with Z can lie in the future.
This request confirmed an intent: amend_intent of that intent first (it clears the confirmation), then act on the request.

route_request.description: Route a current request to an open intent it is part of. Only a request routed to an intent confirms it, names its Lead or waives one of its criteria.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

submission_criteria.message: Name a current request; a superseded one was replaced: use the request that supersedes it.
Name an existing intent (search intent), or draft it with draft_intent from this request.
The intent is met or retired; route the request to an open intent or draft a new one.
This request confirmed an intent: amend_intent of that intent first (it clears the confirmation), then act on the request.

set_request_aside.description: Set a current request aside: it is part of no intent (a remark, a question answered at once). Give the reason; the reference intent is cleared.

request.description: The current request to set aside.

reason.description: Why the request is part of no intent.

submission_criteria.message: Name a current request; a superseded one was replaced: use the request that supersedes it.
Give the reason in words.
This request confirmed an intent: amend_intent of that intent first (it clears the confirmation), then act on the request.

end_delegation.description: The user ends a delegation: the delegation becomes superseded and confirm_intent_delegated refuses it from then on; the intents it confirmed keep it. stopped_by is the user's later word that ended it.

request.description: The current request of kind delegation that the user ends.

stopped_by.description: The user's current order, decision, correction or stop, said after the delegation, that ends it.

submission_criteria.message: Name a current request of kind delegation; a delegation the user ended is superseded.
stopped_by must be a current request of kind order, decision, correction or stop: record the user's word that ends the delegation.
stopped_by must be said after the delegation it ends.

draft_intent.description: Draft an intent from the request that started it; that request is routed to it. The key is the native key of the parameter intent (lower-case letters, digits and -, at most 60 bytes); a used key is refused by the engine (revision_conflict).

intent.description: The new intent: an Id of type intent whose native_key is the new key.

outcome.description: What is true when the intent is met, as sentences that can each be checked true or false.

first_user.description: Who or what uses the result first, and the real run that shows it working.

origin.description: The current request that started the intent; it is routed to the intent.

why.description: Why the user wants it: the need behind the outcome.

not_included.description: What the user does not want done under this intent.

constraints.description: Limits the work keeps: tools, data, cost, time, places not to touch.

questions.description: Open questions to the user, at most five: each with the default the Lead assumes until the user answers, and the answer (empty until answered). Given whole; replaces the list.

directory.description: The task directory of the work for this intent.

submission_criteria.message: Name a current request as origin; record the message first (record_request).
That request confirmed an intent; record the message that starts this intent as its own request.
State the outcome: what is true when the intent is met.
Name who or what uses the result first and the real run that shows it.

amend_intent.description: Change the substance of an open intent: a member given replaces its value, one not given keeps it. The intent returns to draft and its confirmation is cleared: the user confirms it again.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

outcome.description: What is true when the intent is met, as sentences that can each be checked true or false.

first_user.description: Who or what uses the result first, and the real run that shows it working.

why.description: Why the user wants it: the need behind the outcome.

not_included.description: What the user does not want done under this intent.

constraints.description: Limits the work keeps: tools, data, cost, time, places not to touch.

questions.description: Open questions to the user, at most five: each with the default the Lead assumes until the user answers, and the answer (empty until answered). Given whole; replaces the list.

directory.description: The task directory of the work for this intent.

submission_criteria.message: Name an intent that exists and is neither met nor retired; for new work draft a new intent.
An outcome given is not empty; omit it to keep the outcome.
A first_user given is not empty; omit it to keep it.

note_intent.description: Replace the Lead's notes of an open intent for the next Lead; nothing else changes.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

notes.description: The whole new notes: the state, the next step, where things are.

submission_criteria.message: Name an intent that exists and is neither met nor retired; for new work draft a new intent.

name_lead.description: Record the session that leads an open intent, named by the user's request routed to it.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

session.description: The session that leads the work.

by.description: The user's current order, decision or delegation, routed to this intent, that names the Lead.

submission_criteria.message: Name an intent that exists and is neither met nor retired; for new work draft a new intent.
by must be a current request of kind order, decision or delegation: the user's word that names the Lead.
Route the request to this intent first (route_request), then name the Lead with it.

assume_intent.description: The Lead proceeds on a draft intent without the user's confirmation, giving the reason; only an actor with the role lead. The user can still confirm or amend it.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

reason.description: Why the Lead proceeds without the user's confirmation.

submission_criteria.message: Only a draft intent is assumed; amend_intent returns an intent to draft.
Only the Lead does this: apply it with the role lead (ONT_ROLE=lead or the request member role).
Give the reason in words.

confirm_intent.description: Confirm a draft or assumed intent by the user's word: a current order, decision or answer routed to it and said after its last amendment. The intent needs a criterion that is not waived.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

by.description: The user's current order, decision or answer, routed to this intent, that confirms it.

submission_criteria.message: Only a draft or assumed intent is confirmed; a confirmed one is amended first, a closed one stays closed.
by must be a current request of kind order, decision or answer: the user's own word.
Route the request to this intent first (route_request), then confirm with it.
The request was said before the last amendment: the user confirms the intent as it now stands, with a later message.
Add a success criterion first (add_criterion): an intent is confirmed only with one that is not waived.

confirm_intent_delegated.description: The Lead confirms a draft or assumed intent under a current delegation of the user. Route the delegation or set it aside BEFORE its first use: after it, neither is possible. The reason stays in the action log.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

delegation.description: The user's current request of kind delegation that covers this intent.

reason.description: Why the delegation covers this intent.

submission_criteria.message: Only a draft or assumed intent is confirmed; a confirmed one is amended first, a closed one stays closed.
Only the Lead does this: apply it with the role lead (ONT_ROLE=lead or the request member role).
Name a current request of kind delegation; a delegation the user ended is superseded.
Give the reason in words.
Add a success criterion first (add_criterion): an intent is confirmed only with one that is not waived.

close_intent.description: Close a confirmed intent as met once every criterion passed or is waived.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

reason.description: How the outcome was shown: the run or the evidence.

submission_criteria.message: Only a confirmed intent closes as met: have it confirmed first.
Check each open or failed criterion until it passes (check_criterion), or have the user waive it.

retire_intent.description: Retire an intent that is neither met nor retired: the user no longer wants it, or another intent replaces it.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

reason.description: Why the intent is retired; name a replacing intent when there is one.

submission_criteria.message: Name an intent that exists and is neither met nor retired; for new work draft a new intent.
Give the reason in words.

add_criterion.description: Add a success criterion to an open intent: a statement checkable true or false and the check that shows it. It starts open.

intent.description: The intent: its full Id, with the intent's key as native_key.

statement.description: What must be true, checkable as true or false.

check.description: How to check it: the command, the test, the eval with its threshold, or the real run to observe.

baseline.description: For a number: its value before the work, with its source and time.

submission_criteria.message: Name an intent that exists and is neither met nor retired; for new work draft a new intent.
State what must be true.
Say how the statement is checked.

check_criterion.description: Record the result of a criterion's check: pass or fail, with the evidence. A later check replaces it.

evidence.description: The command and its result, or what was observed.

submission_criteria.message: state is pass or fail; a criterion is waived only by waive_criterion.
Give the evidence: the command and its result.
Name an existing criterion that is not waived; a waived criterion keeps its state.

waive_criterion.description: The user waives a criterion: name the user's request, routed to the criterion's intent, that says so, and the reason. The reason becomes the evidence.

by.description: The user's current decision, order or answer, routed to the criterion's intent, that waives it.

reason.description: Why the criterion no longer has to pass.

submission_criteria.message: by must be a current request of kind decision, order or answer: the user's own word.
Route the request to the criterion's intent first (route_request), then waive with it.
Give the reason in words.
